transcript:
anna: Heads-up: shadowbench shows weird behavior after per-layer dynamic quant (PTQ layer-wise scale). NDCG ~unchanged but MRR for short queries (<=5 tokens) drops ~6%. Anyone else hit this? :thinking:

mike: Can you paste the exact eval slice and config? short-query drift is usually trickier with kvpack/priming.

anna: Sure — eval slice = short_queries_v2 (n=8k), candidates=100, measure=MRR@10/NDCG@10. Quant config: `dynquant_per_layer=true`, `clip_bits=4` on activations only, `outlier_threshold=3.5`.

josh: Do we have tokenizer parity between offline eval and production? small tokenization shifts can flip MRR for short prompts.

anna: Tokenizer parity check = pass. Also ran a control with float32 weights but same tokenizer and candidate ordering; no drop.

sara: Any change in candidate ordering or dedupe before scoring? That can silently move the ground truth around topk.

anna: No ordering changes. I compared raw scorer logits for a handful of failing queries — logits for the correct candidate are lower after quant for short queries.

mike: Can you share a tiny repro pair (query + candidate) that flips? we can run quick per-layer scale debug.

anna: Pasting one example:
```
query: "how to reset npm cache"
candA (correct): "npm cache clean --force"
candB: "npm uninstall npm -g"
float32_logits: [candA: 3.21, candB: 1.12]
int4_logits:   [candA: 1.02, candB: 1.08]
```

josh: Interesting — absolute drop on correct candidate, others stable. Suggests per-layer scale clipping hitting certain feature directions.

eval-bot: New run finished 1708501123. Slice: short_queries_v2. MRR@10: float=0.421, int4_dyn=0.395, delta=-0.026. NDCG@10 delta=-0.003. CI overlap? barely.

sara: Maybe try layerwise symmetric vs asymmetric scaling and compare. Also check fp16 quant baseline (if available) to isolate activation clipping vs weight quant.

anna: Will run quick ablation: (1) symmetric vs asymmetric per-layer scale (2) widen outlier threshold to 5.0 (3) per-layer bias correction pass.

mike: Also run a targeted gradient-approx PTQ (loss-based) on a small calibration set of short queries. If loss prioritizes short-query directions it might preserve MRR.

josh: Could also be candidate length bias — shorter candidates amplify small logit shifts. Add candidate-length as slice.

anna: Good idea. I'll add candidate-length bucket and run 3 ablations + grad-ptq. ETA ~2h. Posting results here when ready. :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks — if this reproduces, we should add a short-query golden set to the onboarding checklist for future quant configs.

anna: Agree. Adding to onboarding TODO list: "golden_shortquery_set for PTQ sanity". I'll open a brief PR with the checklist and link back to this thread.

eval-bot: Note: include random seeds in runs to help reproduce nondeterminism (seed=42 used in float run, int4 run used seed=7).
